newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads pressured, EchoStar dips.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads pressured, EchoStar dips.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate bond spreads were under pressure to widen on Monday as prospective supply and interest rate uncertainties loomed, traders said.
High-yielding issues were unchanged to slightly better, meanwhile, with the exception of downward price adjustments to debt of EchoStar Communications Corp, traders said.
EchoStar debt turned sharply lower after the company said the planned $1.0 billion investment by News Corp Ltd in the satellite broadcaster had been delayed, traders and analysts said.

News Corp on Friday indicated it will not proceed with the investment unless EchoStar abandons its existing system of consumer access to satellite-delivered television programs in favor of a News Corp affiliated system. The delivery of new conditions delayed News Corp's application for regulatory approval beyond the end of April as planned, EchoStar said.

EchoStar's 12-7/8 percent senior secured discount notes due 2004 traded off three points to 83 bid, according to traders. EchoStar's subordinated debt was quoted off more than five points in a 74 bid, 77 offer market near the close.

Despite the losses, analysts said the News Corp ultimatum suggests the deal will be re-worked but not abandoned. In fact, KDP Investment Advisors analyst Eric Tutterow said the reaction was overdone and reiterated a buy recommendation.
Elsewhere, Pathmark Stores 9-5/8 percent debt extended recent losses and fell more than one point to a 90-3/4 bid, 91-1/2 offer market.

But market tone maintained improvements seen over the past week, although volume was thin. Dealers said investors were looking ahead to approximately $1 billion in new junk issues to affirm the new-found market stability.

In the high-grade arena, spreads were unchanged to two basis points wider in light trading ahead of some big new issues and the release of potent economic data, traders said. Tobacco paper underperformed the market, they added.
"People were just reluctant to get involved today because of the calendar," one trader said.
Leading supply, General Motors Acceptance Corp issued $500 million four-year 7-1/8 percent notes to yield 40 basis points over Treasuries via lead manager Lehman Brothers.
And in junk rated issues, Bank United Corp issued $220 million Ba3/BB-plus 8-7/8 percent subordinated notes to yield 200 basis points over Treasuries via a Smith Barney Inc syndicate.

Turning to U.S. Treasuries, prices popped following a Federal Reserve coupon pass totaling nearly $2 billion. But prices had been mostly static ahead data including the government's quarterly Employment Cost Index on Tuesday and April non-farm payrolls on Friday.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed up 11/32 at 93-31/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
